caption:
Hashtags do not increase your reach. Not a hot take — Mosseri said it out loud, and Instagram capped hashtags at five per post in December 2025.

So what are 30 hashtags doing in your caption? Telling Instagram what the post is about and helping it show in search. That's the whole job. Every hour spent building hashtag sets, rotating them, or hiding them in the first comment bought you nothing in distribution.

The other half of this is bigger. Repost other people's content ten or more times in 30 days and Instagram removes your account from recommendations entirely. Since April 30, 2026, accounts that mostly post other people's content are out. Your followers still see you. Strangers stop.

For anyone running a page built on reposted clips: that's the whole growth engine, switched off.

The flip side is the opportunity. Instagram recommends the original version. Being the person who made the thing is now a distribution advantage, not just a moral one — and "original" is a lower bar than it sounds. Your own face, your own screen recording, your own client story, your own numbers.

Badly shot and yours beats polished and borrowed.
